andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh steps up El Niño response with crop-protection and essential-commodity measures
facts: On 20 September, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a teleconference with senior officials and district collectors to review El Niño impacts and response measures.
The Chief Minister said the State had recorded a rainfall deficit of more than 50%; agricultural operations had begun over 79% of the area.
Officials were directed to release rice stocks from storage into the market and take steps to control prices of rice, onions, palm oil and red gram.
The government was asked to increase onion procurement and encourage cultivation to meet future demand.
The directives combine agricultural support with food-supply and price-monitoring measures during Kharif 2026.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Andhra Pradesh had already been tracking El Niño-related Kharif stress and drought preparedness. Today: the Chief Minister’s teleconference added immediate market-supply directions, including releasing rice stocks and increasing onion procurement, alongside continued farmer-support measures.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Agricultural risk management, drought preparedness, food security and state disaster governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish a reported rainfall deficit and preparedness directions from a formal drought declaration; the 20 September measures included rice-stock release and onion procurement.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how climate-risk planning can integrate crop protection, food-price stabilisation, water security and interdepartmental coordination.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct Andhra Pradesh connection: State-level Kharif conditions, district collectors and State food-supply measures.

| **Onions** | Control prices; increase procurement and encourage cultivation to meet future demand |

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh orders interim special-officer administration for Zilla and Mandal Praja Parishads
facts: The Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department issued G.O. Ms. Nos. 128 and 129 on 19 September under Section 250-A of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
The elected Mandal Praja Parishad bodies are due to complete their terms on 23 September; the Zilla Praja Parishad bodies are due to complete their terms on 24 September.
District Collectors and District Magistrates are to act as special officers for Zilla Praja Parishads from 25 September.
Collectors are authorised to appoint special officers to Mandal Praja Parishads from 24 September; appointees are to be district-level officers at least one rank above the MPDO, excluding engineers.
The special-officer arrangement is for up to six months or until elected office-bearers assume office, whichever occurs earlier.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State issued orders for interim administration as elected rural local-body terms approach expiry. The orders provide for Collectors to administer Zilla Praja Parishads and for Collectors to appoint eligible district-level officers to Mandal Praja Parishads until elected bodies assume office or the six-month period ends.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: 73rd Constitutional Amendment, rural local self-government and continuity of administration under state Panchayat Raj law.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Section 250-A of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, provides for special officers when the election process is not completed; the order specifies a maximum six-month term or earlier transition to elected office-bearers.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how temporary administrative arrangements can maintain local-body functions while raising questions about democratic continuity and timely elections.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct Andhra Pradesh connection: the orders apply to State Zilla Praja Parishads and Mandal Praja Parishads, including the newly formed districts.

andhraPradesh.headline: IMD forecasts very heavy to extremely heavy rain over north coastal Andhra Pradesh
facts: The India Meteorological Department’s 20 September bulletin reported a low-pressure area over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining north Andaman Sea.
IMD forecast that the system could intensify into a depression on 21 September and a deep depression on 22 September, approaching the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast around 23 September.
Heavy to very heavy rainfall was forecast over north coastal Andhra Pradesh from 22–24 September, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall possible on 23–24 September.
Squally winds of 55–65 km/h were forecast along and off the south Odisha–north Andhra Pradesh coasts on 23 September, likely continuing until the evening of 24 September.
These were forecasts issued on 20 September, not reports of rainfall subsequently observed.
andhraPradesh.summary: IMD issued a coastal-weather warning as a Bay of Bengal low-pressure system was forecast to intensify and approach the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast. The bulletin forecast very heavy to isolated extremely heavy rain and squally winds; these conditions were prospective as of the issue date.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Bay of Bengal weather systems, monsoon dynamics, coastal hazards and early-warning-based disaster management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The 20 September IMD bulletin forecast heavy to very heavy rain in north coastal Andhra Pradesh during 22–24 September and isolated extremely heavy rain on 23–24 September.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how forecast-led district preparedness, coastal communication and protection of exposed communities can reduce risks from severe rainfall and squally winds.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct Andhra Pradesh connection: the forecast specifically covered north coastal Andhra Pradesh and the State’s coastal waters.

andhraPradesh.headline: India announces ninth International Water Week on climate-resilient water management
facts: The Ministry of Jal Shakti announced that the ninth India International Water Week would run from 22 to 26 September 2026.
The announced venue was Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; the theme was “Climate Resilient Water Management.”
The Ministry of Jal Shakti is organising the event with Central Ministries, State Governments, international organisations, research and academic institutions, industry and development partners.
The event was announced as a multidisciplinary platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange, innovation and partnerships on water challenges.
The 20 September announcement concerned a scheduled event; it did not establish Andhra Pradesh’s participation or any State-specific outcome.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti announced the five-day ninth India International Water Week for 22–26 September in New Delhi. Its stated focus is climate-resilient water management and exchange among government, research, industry and international participants.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Integrated water resources management, climate adaptation and cooperative federalism in water governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Ninth India International Water Week 2026: 22–26 September, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; theme—“Climate Resilient Water Management.”
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Relate water-sector collaboration to climate adaptation, demand management and the need to connect national dialogue with State-level water security planning.

andhraPradesh.headline: World Cleanup Day 2026 highlights food waste and circular, cleaner cities
facts: World Cleanup Day is observed annually on 20 September; the 2026 global observance was held in Shaoxing, Zhejiang Province, China.
The 2026 theme was “From Clean Plates to Clean Cities,” linking food-waste prevention with cleaner, more resource-efficient cities.
The United Nations page calls for keeping edible food in use, recovering unavoidable organic material and reducing waste.
The UN page cites the UNEP Food Waste Index 2024 estimate that about 1.05 billion metric tonnes of food were wasted at household, food-service and retail levels in 2022.
andhraPradesh.summary: The 2026 global observance focused on food waste as a city-scale environmental and resource-management challenge. Its theme linked household and food-system choices with waste prevention and circular urban systems.

national.headline: 13th SLINEX-26 underway at Visakhapatnam
facts: SLINEX-26 is the 13th edition of the Sri Lanka–India bilateral maritime exercise.
The exercise is being conducted at Visakhapatnam from 17 to 21 September 2026.
India’s participants include INS Kavaratti, an indigenous anti-submarine warfare corvette, and fleet tanker INS Jyoti; Sri Lanka is represented by SLNS Sindurala.
The harbour phase includes professional interactions and cross-deck visits; the sea phase is intended to strengthen operational coordination and interoperability.
The exercise is aligned with India’s MAHASAGAR vision.
national.summary: The 13th edition of the India–Sri Lanka maritime exercise is ongoing at Visakhapatnam, with harbour activities followed by a sea phase. It provides a practical setting for naval cooperation and maritime interoperability between the two countries.

national.headline: Indian shooters win two silver medals on opening day of Asian Games shooting
facts: At the 20th Asian Games in Aichi–Nagoya, India won silver in the women’s 10m air rifle team event on 20 September.
Sonam Uttam Maskar, Elavenil Valarivan and Vidarsa Kochalumkal Vinod scored 1,898.0; China won gold with 1,904.2 and Japan won bronze with 1,897.1.
Elavenil Valarivan also won silver in the individual women’s 10m air rifle final with 252.4 points.
Japan’s Hinata Taichi won individual gold with an Asian Games record of 253.0; South Korea’s Ban Hyojin took bronze.
China set a world record of 1,904.2 in the women’s 10m air rifle team qualification competition.
national.summary: Previous: the Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games opening was covered on 19 September. Today: Indian shooters secured team and individual silver medals in women’s 10m air rifle; the International Shooting Sport Federation recorded the event results and the Asian Games record in the individual final.

national.headline: NGT climate conference concludes with call for community-centred resilience
facts: The National Green Tribunal’s two-day international conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” concluded in New Delhi on 20 September.
President Droupadi Murmu addressed the valedictory session and advocated people-centred, community-based climate adaptation rooted in traditional knowledge.
The conference brought together participants from 17 countries, with representatives of UNEP and the Asian Development Bank among those attending.
Union Minister Manohar Lal released the NGT commemorative book Harit Nyayam and presented its first copy to the President.
The conference called for translating environmental commitments into practical action, stronger institutions and continued international cooperation.
national.summary: Previous: the conference was inaugurated on 19 September. Today: it concluded with the President’s valedictory address, and the NGT’s commemorative book Harit Nyayam was released. The discussions linked climate resilience with environmental governance, community participation and cooperation across jurisdictions.
national.staticLink: National Green Tribunal, environmental governance and climate adaptation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The NGT organised the conference in New Delhi; UNEP is the United Nations Environment Programme, and the commemorative book released was Harit Nyayam.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how environmental adjudication, local knowledge and community participation can strengthen climate adaptation and environmental justice.

- **Venue:** **New Delhi**
- **Participation:** Representatives from **17 countries**, including **UNEP** and the **Asian Development Bank**

# 2. Dignitaries and book
- **Valedictory address:** **President Droupadi Murmu** advocated people-centred, community-based climate adaptation rooted in traditional knowledge
- **Book:** **Harit Nyayam**, the NGT commemorative book
- **Released by:** **Union Minister Manohar Lal**; first copy presented to **President Droupadi Murmu**

national.headline: Government reports 5.69 lakh ODF Plus villages under rural sanitation programme
facts: A PIB backgrounder published on 20 September reported rural sanitation figures as of 17 September 2026.
India had 5.69 lakh ODF Plus villages, including 5.25 lakh classified as ODF Plus Model villages.
Solid-waste management arrangements were reported in 5.38 lakh villages and liquid-waste management systems in 5.65 lakh villages.
The government reported 1,314 operational GOBARdhan biogas plants across 582 districts.
GOBARdhan supports conversion of cattle dung, crop residue and organic waste into biogas, compressed biogas and organic manure or bio-slurry.
national.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti’s published backgrounder provided a nationwide update on rural sanitation outcomes, with the underlying village figures stated as of 17 September. It also described ODF Plus as extending beyond toilet access to sustained sanitation and solid- and liquid-waste management.
national.staticLink: Swachh Bharat Mission–Gramin Phase II, sanitation governance and decentralised waste management.
national.prelimsTakeaway: ODF Plus Model villages manage both solid and liquid waste and maintain visual cleanliness; GOBARdhan promotes productive use of organic waste.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate the shift from toilet construction to sustained sanitation outcomes, local waste systems and behaviour change in rural development.

national.headline: Central Silk Board marks 77th Foundation Day; national silk output target set at 60,000 tonnes
facts: The Central Silk Board held its 77th Foundation Day programme and an exhibition of silk products and technologies in Bengaluru on 20 September.
The Union Textiles Minister stated that India’s silk production had risen from 26,000 metric tonnes in 2014 to 42,000 metric tonnes.
A target of 60,000 metric tonnes of silk production by 2030–31 was announced; the stated ambition is to reach the world’s top position in silk production by 2028–29.
The Ministry said high-yielding silkworm hybrids and machinery, alongside AI, GIS and machine-learning applications, are being introduced to support production and quality.
Silk farmers and weavers from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu participated; the event also included appointment letters for 28 scientists.
national.summary: The Foundation Day programme highlighted national sericulture production targets and technology priorities for the silk value chain. The stated production and global-ranking goals are targets, not achieved results; participants included farmers and weavers from Andhra Pradesh.

international.headline: UN General Assembly’s 81st High-Level Week underway amid conflicts, AI and climate concerns
facts: The 81st UN General Assembly High-Level Week is scheduled for 18–28 September 2026 in New York.
The UN General Debate is scheduled for 22–28 September under the theme “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.”
Reuters reported that nearly 130 heads of state were gathering for the week, with conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and AI risks prominent in discussions.
The UN programme also includes high-level events on climate action and the just transition, sea-level rise, and pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.

international.headline: US proposes AI-incident notification mechanism in talks with China
facts: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded talks in New York on 20 September.
The US proposed a bilateral AI dialogue with a notification mechanism for AI-related incidents serious enough to raise national-security concerns.
The proposal was for the leaders of the two countries to consider; the talks did not produce a concluded AI agreement.
US officials said advanced AI-chip and semiconductor-equipment export controls were not part of the proposed mechanism.
international.summary: The US put forward a proposal for Washington and Beijing to share notifications about serious AI-related security incidents. The proposal remained under consideration, rather than constituting an agreed bilateral mechanism.
international.staticLink: International technology governance; AI safety; confidence-building measures and strategic relations.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The proposed mechanism concerns notification of AI incidents with national-security implications; it is distinct from semiconductor export controls.
international.mainsAngle: Examine the scope and limits of bilateral AI-risk communication as a confidence-building measure between strategic competitors.

international.headline: India women reach Asian Games cricket final after 114-run win over Bangladesh
facts: In the women’s cricket semi-final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin, India defeated Bangladesh by 114 runs.
India scored 195/4; Shafali Verma made 100, her maiden T20I century, and Smriti Mandhana scored 37.
Bangladesh were dismissed for 81; India advanced to the gold-medal match against Sri Lanka, scheduled for 22 September.
Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan by eight wickets in the other semi-final.

international.headline: Canada and France set priorities for cooperation on space, energy security and climate resilience
facts: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met French President Emmanuel Macron in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon on 20 September.
The leaders directed their space agencies, defence ministries and industries to develop and share space infrastructure, including launch systems and ground reception and control infrastructure.
They tasked the Regional Joint Cooperation Commission with expanding work on trade diversification, energy transition, climate resilience and early-warning systems, and cross-border security.
The visit was the first official visit by a Canadian prime minister to Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, according to the Canadian government.
international.summary: The leaders outlined expanded Canada–France cooperation, including a direction to develop shared space infrastructure and new priorities for their regional cooperation commission. The Canadian government described the visit as the first official visit by a Canadian prime minister to the French archipelago.
international.staticLink: Bilateral relations; space cooperation; energy security; climate resilience; geography of Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon is a French territory in the North Atlantic near Canada; the leaders’ announced space-infrastructure work was a direction to develop cooperation, not a completed project.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how bilateral and regional partnerships can build resilience through cooperation on space, energy, climate adaptation and security.
